name: Seismic horizon tracking via deep relative geologic time (RGT): Geng et al. 2020 (2D CNN RGT), Wu et al. 2020 (realistic synthetic structure models for CNN training), Bi et al. 2021 (Deep RGT, 3D attention U-Net + structural-similarity loss), Yang et al. 2023 (transformer multi-task RGT/horizons/faults with horizon priors), Dou et al. 2026 (RGT-Est, sinusoidal-phase RGT); plus pretrain-to-alignment RGT (2026)

(USTC Computational Interpretation Group, CIG); Zhengfa Bi, Xinming Wu, Zhicheng Geng, Haishan Li (USTC / UT Austin / PetroChina NWGI); Jiarun Yang, Xinming Wu et al. Wu 2020: Geophysics 85(4) WA27-WA39, 'Building realistic structure models to train convolutional neural networks for seismic structural interpretation' [uncertain that this is the 'Wu 2020' intended by the outline]. code_availability: Yes: Bi 2021 rgtNet (PyTorch, Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/5090317, GitHub zfbi/rgtNet); Dou 2026 RGT-Est with weights on Zenodo (https://github.com/douyimin/RGT-Est, PyTorch Lightning, mixed precision); field fine-tuning code jiarunyangustc/rgt_finetune (https://github.com/jiarunyangustc/rgt_finetune). Geng 2020 and Yang 2023 code [uncertain].
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (Geophysics, JGR Solid Earth, IEEE TGRS) for 2020-2023; arXiv preprints for 2026 work. Field results are mostly qualitative (visual horizon alignment); no well-log / geosteering evaluation. Transfer to ROGII is our analysis.
extreme_summary: Instead of tracking each horizon, a network regresses one scalar field (relative geologic time) over the whole seismic image; every horizon is an iso-contour of that field, so all horizons are mutually consistent (non-crossing, ordered) by construction, and faults appear as RGT discontinuities. Later work adds structure-aware losses (SSIM, perceptual, adversarial), sparse horizon priors, and multi-frequency sinusoidal encodings of RGT that make closely spaced, similar-looking layers distinguishable.
task_definition: From a 2D seismic section or 3D seismic volume, predict at every sample the relative geologic time (stratigraphic age / depositional order), then extract horizons as RGT iso-surfaces and faults as lateral RGT discontinuities; optional sparse interpreted horizons as constraints.
inputs: Seismic amplitude image / volume; optionally sparse horizon picks (2D lines or 3D surfaces) as prior channels (Yang 2023, Dou 2026); fault labels in multi-task setups. ROGII analogue: the lateral-vs-typewell GR cost image over (MD column x TVT level), with the heel prefix as the sparse 'horizon pick'.
target_parameterisation: Relative geologic time: a scalar field monotonically increasing with depth along each vertical trace (monotonicity not hard-enforced by the networks); Dou 2026 maps the scalar RGT r in [-1, 1] to three sinusoidal channels sin/cos-style at frequencies 2.0, 1.0, 0.5 and optimises in that phase space as well as on the scalar. ROGII analogue: TVT along the lateral is exactly an RGT sample (stratigraphic depth of the bit), and S = TVT + Z is the structural elevation of a reference horizon at each MD.
output_representation: Dense scalar field (point regression per pixel/voxel); horizons derived as iso-contours; no per-pixel distribution or multiple hypotheses.
architecture: Geng 2020: 2D ResNet-50 encoder + U-Net-style decoder + refinement module. Bi 2021: simplified 3D U-shaped encoder-decoder with multi-scale residual learning and attention (channel/spatial highlighting), plus a sub-volume-then-merge workflow to handle large volumes without boundary artefacts. Yang 2023: transformer-based multi-task network with shared features and two mutually constraining branches (RGT, faults), lighter than CNNs with larger structure-oriented receptive field, horizon priors as input. Dou 2026: 3D HRNet (parallel multi-resolution branches), optional sparse 2D/3D horizon guidance channel, output RGT in [-1, 1] then sinusoidal transform, 3D PatchGAN discriminator conditioned on seismic.
core_mechanism: (1) Global scalar-field parameterisation: predicting one field whose level sets are the horizons couples all horizons and all traces, giving built-in stratigraphic consistency and fault-crossing correlation without explicit tracking. (2) Structure-aware losses (Bi's structural-similarity loss; Dou's multi-directional 3D LPIPS and adversarial loss) supervise spatial relationships rather than independent pixels, countering over-smoothing. (3) Dou's multi-frequency sinusoidal phase targets amplify small RGT differences (reported ~62x larger L1 gradients) so thin, similar layers get distinct codes while the low-frequency channel removes wrap-around ambiguity. (4) Sparse horizon priors pin the field where interpretations exist. (5) Heavy synthetic training from forward-modelled folded/faulted structure models (Wu 2020 generator line).
training_objective: Geng 2020: pixel-wise MSE. Bi 2021: structural-similarity (SSIM-based) criterion to capture spatial dependencies. Yang 2023: multi-task RGT regression + fault segmentation with shared features [uncertain on exact weights]. Dou 2026: lambda_reg=5 x (L1/L2 on scalar RGT + L1 on phase representation) + lambda_lpips=5 x multi-directional 3D LPIPS (32 slices per axis) + lambda_adv=0.01 x relativistic hinge adversarial loss.
decoding: Direct regression output; horizons = iso-contours of the predicted RGT; faults = lateral discontinuities of RGT.
metric_consistent_decode: Scalar MSE regression estimates the conditional mean (RMSE-consistent); SSIM/LPIPS and especially the adversarial term are distribution-matching / mode-seeking and favour sharp single hypotheses, which would raise pooled RMSE under band ambiguity.
evidence_scope: Whole 2D section or 3D volume (large receptive field; sub-volume stitching in Bi 2021); single survey, no multi-survey joint inference.
prefix_conditioning: Sparse interpreted horizons as extra input channels (Yang 2023; Dou 2026 shows 2D/3D horizon constraints significantly improve precision and lateral consistency). Direct analogue of our known heel TVT prefix.
propose_vs_select: Single output field; no candidate generation. Could be an auxiliary head or target reparameterisation rather than a separate ensemble member.
physical_constraints: Consistency and ordering of horizons implied by the scalar-field formulation; monotonicity with depth is NOT hard-enforced (Dou 2026 lists lack of hard monotonicity / non-intersection constraints as a limitation); faults as discontinuities; SSIM/LPIPS/adversarial terms as soft structural priors.
dataset: Geng 2020: 2,080 synthetic 2D seismic/RGT training pairs, 960 test images, field sections. Bi 2021: thousands of noisy synthetic 3D seismic/RGT volumes (rgtNet repo cites 400 training pairs) [uncertain on exact count] plus three field volumes. Dou 2026: 2,000 synthetic 512^3 volume pairs (faults, unconformities, folds, clinoforms), field surveys from Costa Rica, Poseidon (Australia), Netherlands F3, China. Pretrain-to-alignment 2026: validated on 3,000 field datasets across basins (shelf-edge clinothems).
synthetic_to_real: All core methods train purely on synthetic data generated from structural models (Wu 2020 line: flat layers + folding + faulting + wavelet convolution + noise) and apply zero-shot to field data. The 2026 pretrain-to-alignment paper argues this leaves a synthetic-to-field gap and proposes four stages: self-supervised pretraining on field data, synthetic supervision, prior-driven refinement, and domain-adaptation fine-tuning on scarce field labels; jiarunyangustc/rgt_finetune fine-tunes a pretrained RGT net on field data with multi-source constraints.
metric_and_performance: Mostly qualitative on field data (horizon alignment with reflectors, preserved ordering in weak-reflection zones, faults). Synthetic test metrics (MSE / SSIM / R2) reported in Geng and Bi [uncertain on exact values]. Dou 2026 reports ~62x (L1) and ~16x (LPIPS) gradient amplification in sinusoidal vs raw space and improved horizon alignment over voxel-space baselines, without a standard numeric benchmark.
comparability: Not comparable: seismic RGT fields vs well-log TVT RMSE on 155 holdout wells; no shared metric.
validation_protocol: Synthetic held-out sets plus visual checks on field surveys; no spatially grouped CV concept. Weak quantitative evidence for field gains.
inference_budget: 3D volumes at 512^3 need large GPUs, but the ROGII analogue is a 1D path per well or our existing 345 x 400 image, so any transplanted head / loss adds negligible inference cost.
repeated_layers: Handled in principle by global context (the whole section constrains which reflector is which) and, in Dou 2026, by multi-frequency phase codes: high frequency separates thin layers locally, low frequency tells which cycle, avoiding wrap-around. This mirrors our band confusion: GR repeats with a quasi-period, so 'position within the cycle' is easy and 'which cycle' is the hard part. None of these works outputs a distribution, so ambiguity is resolved by regression toward the mean (or sharpened by adversarial loss).
drift: RGT fields are driven by global structural consistency and by sparse horizon priors; smooth structural dip is implicit in the synthetic folding models. The ROGII analogue of drift is a wrong dip of the structural surface S(MD); a gradient-consistency view of RGT suggests supervising the derivative dS/dMD (dip) directly, which is not done in our pipeline (see gap).
uncertainty_and_calibration: None: point regression without uncertainty or calibration analysis; limitations sections note unreliable predictions where reflectors are obscured.
where_to_use: (1) Loss / target design in the ConvNeXt / FastViT U-Net: an RGT-style supervised dip (gradient) consistency loss on the expected path's structural surface S = E[TVT] + Z over multiple MD windows; and an auxiliary multi-frequency sinusoidal head (sin/cos of 2*pi*TVT/P_k) sharing the decoder. (2) Training schedule: a pretrain-to-alignment style final stage on real wells only after the 85%-synthetic phase. (3) Conceptual: treat the heel prefix like sparse horizon priors (already done via tvt_input channels) and neighbour wells like a multi-trace RGT field (belongs to A12).
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25%) via dip-consistency supervision and real-data alignment; band confusion (~51%) weakly via multi-frequency auxiliary targets (feature learning) and via synthetic-to-real alignment.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Checked in kaggle_1st_place/solution: (a) Our output is a per-column softmax over 400 TVT levels with expectation decode - already RGT-like (TVT is a relative stratigraphic coordinate) but column-wise; path-level consistency comes only from receptive field. (b) The 1st-place code already has a structural-surface loss, 'dS_penalty' (masked_surface_curvature_l1_loss in experiments/arch/seq_NN_train.py): an unsupervised L1 penalty on the second difference of S = pred_TVT + z_rel, with cfg dS_windows (1, 7, 15, 31); its weight is 0.0 in unet_loss_weights in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py, i.e. switched off in our runs. What is missing entirely is a SUPERVISED multi-window slope-matching term, |dS_pred/dMD - dS_true/dMD| averaged over windows 7-63 columns, which is the RGT-gradient analogue and directly penalises the one-straight-line-per-well drift (per-well linear trend removal is worth 4.94 -> 3.07 ft on ConvNeXt). (c) No multi-frequency / phase auxiliary target exists; targets are 'alignment' (smoothed one-hot over levels), 'regression', 'GR_penalty'. (d) Structural losses of SSIM / LPIPS / adversarial type are absent - correctly so for RMSE, since adversarial terms are mode-seeking. (e) A 'finetune' stage exists (finetune_epochs, finetune_lr_reduce=0.3, disables z_shift aug) but whether it trains on real wells only, as pretrain-to-alignment recommends, is [uncertain]; our runs use finetune_epochs=None by default. (f) Horizon-prior conditioning is already present in spirit (prefix TVT as tvt_input channels).
proposed_experiment: E1 (lowest effort, targets drift): add a supervised dip-consistency loss 'dS_match' next to dS_penalty in experiments/arch/seq_NN_train.py: S_pred = E_p[TVT] + z_rel, S_true = TVT + z_rel; loss = mean over windows w in (7, 15, 31, 63) of masked L1 of (S_pred[t+w] - S_pred[t]) - (S_true[t+w] - S_true[t]), scaled by surface_stats; weight sweep {0.01, 0.03} x the alignment weight. Config: new key in unet_loss_weights in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py. Run first as a cheap 60-epoch ConvNeXt screen against the 5.47 ft baseline with the same seed, then 150-epoch teacher -> FastViT-SA12 distillation vs the 4.84 ft student. Metrics: pooled RMSE via seq_NN_holdout_eval.py, paired bootstrap via seq_NN_robust_compare.py, AND the per-well linear-trend residual decomposition (does the drift share fall?). Also run a control with the existing dS_penalty switched on (weight 0.01) to separate unsupervised smoothness from supervised dip matching. E2 (targets synthetic-to-real gap): pretrain-to-alignment stage - after the 150-epoch mixed run, continue 15-20 epochs on real training wells only (synthetic ratio 0), LR x0.3, z_shift off (use the existing finetune_* machinery if it can be restricted to real wells); control: 15-20 extra epochs of the same mixed schedule, so epoch count is matched. E3 (targets band confusion via features): auxiliary head of 2K channels predicting sin/cos(2*pi*TVT/P_k), P_k in {8, 32, 128} ft (or P set from the typewell GR autocorrelation period per well), L1 loss weight 0.02, decode unchanged (expectation of the softmax); measure wrong_mode share and pooled RMSE vs control. Run E1 and E2 before E3.
implementation_effort: Low for E1 (about 30 lines beside masked_surface_curvature_l1_loss, one config key); low-medium for E2 (dataset filter for real-only wells plus schedule; check what the finetune path does); medium for E3 (new head, target construction, loss, KD plumbing for the extra head).
gpu_cost: E1: one 60-epoch screen plus one 150-epoch teacher and student run on the RTX 5060 8 GB (same cost as any baseline run, loss overhead negligible). E2: +15-20 epochs on ~15% of the data volume, roughly 10-15% of a full run [uncertain]. E3: small head, <5% memory overhead, one full run.
distillation_compatibility: Yes. E1 and E3 are training losses usable for teacher and student (the student can take dS_match on its own expected path alongside KD on posteriors); E2 applies to the teacher, the student, or both. Nothing changes the output posterior format.
error_correlation_with_ours: Low diversity: these are modifications of our own model, not an independent member; a dS_match-trained model may however drift differently (smaller per-well slope bias) and so could lower the best-pair RMSE if its residual correlation with the current student drops.
risk: (1) Dip supervision may just trade drift for more wrong-band blending: the expectation path under a bimodal posterior has a spurious slope when mass shifts between bands, and the loss would push mass shifts to be smoother rather than correct. (2) Per-column CE on alignment targets already supervises the path densely; the extra term may be redundant and inside the +-0.39 ft noise floor (60-epoch structural changes AcfNet target, axial attention, RAFT all failed). (3) Real-only fine-tuning risks overfitting to ~600 real wells and losing the synthetic-induced robustness; spatial leakage between neighbouring real wells can inflate apparent gains. (4) Sinusoidal auxiliary targets encode position, not evidence: band confusion falls only with more evidence or better calibration (context metric fact), so E3 helps only if it improves features. (5) Seismic RGT evidence is mostly qualitative, so there are no hard numbers to expect a gain size from.
notes: Strong conceptual analogy: ROGII TVT is an RGT value sampled along the well path, and our cost image in (MD, TVT) coordinates is effectively a flattened (RGT-domain) section. The 'monotone RGT-like output parameterisation' in the outline's why-field does not transfer literally - TVT along a lateral is not monotone because the bit moves up and down through strata; the transferable invariant is smoothness of the structural surface S = TVT + Z (dip), which is what E1 supervises. Repeating reflectors in seismic are handled by global context rather than a special mechanism; Dou 2026's multi-frequency phase encoding is the closest to an explicit repeated-layer device. A multi-well RGT field (all laterals and typewells in an area mapped into one geologic-time field) is the principled version of the failed XY geo-prior and belongs to A12. Pretrain-to-alignment also informs B11 (synthetic data / sim-to-real).
